summary: Frontend-only test of the new /process page with Playwright at 1920, 768 and 390 widths. Every requested check passed: / redirects to /process; the 5 sections render in order (hero, at-a-glance, step-by-step, comparison, closing-cta); hero h1 has '[OWNER FIRST NAME]' and span.text-primary 'start to finish'; at-a-glance ol has 3 li showing 01/02/03 with uppercase h3 and the wrapper uses max-w-5xl px-5 py-16 md:py-24; step-by-step ol has 4 rows labeled Day 1 / Days 2–4 / Days 3–10 / Delivery day with 3 bullets each, and '[CONFIRM: FICO floor]' is present; comparison is a semantic table (3 thead th, 6 tbody rows, th scope=row) with header 'Working with [BRAND NAME]' and the brand highlighted in the H2; at 390px the wrapper scrolls (scrollWidth 680 vs clientWidth 348) and the document has no horizontal overflow (390 = 390), and none at 768 either; ClosingCTA goes to /contact#get-started and scrolls to the section; Pre-Qualify secondary has target=_blank rel='noopener noreferrer' and the partner URL; document.title is 'The Process | [BRAND NAME] AUTO' (exactly one <title>) and the meta description is present; there are no forms or inputs on the page; /entrepreneur-loan, /calculator and /contact still render with header and footer; no console errors.

issues: Optional UX suggestion: when the table is scrolled sideways, the row-label column (Pricing visibility, etc.) scrolls out of view. Making the tbody th sticky (sticky left-0 bg-background) would keep the context visible. Not required by the spec.

critical_code_review_comments:
PageHero gives the intro

data-testid '{id}-page-placeholder' (process-page-placeholder). This is left over from the placeholder scaffold. Consider renaming it to '{id}-hero-intro' (only if no other tests rely on it).
The code is clean: content is separated into processContent.js, the components are small, and brand/owner come from site.js.
